title: Derived-complete module complexes are closed under products and triangles
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $I\subseteq A$ be any ideal, and work in $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived completeness means [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex]. (1) If $(K_n)_{n\geq1}$ is a countable family of derived $I$-complete objects, its product $\prod_{n\geq1}K_n$ [def-weil-category-product] is derived $I$-complete. (2) In any distinguished triangle $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$ [def-weil-triangulated-category], if two of $X,Y,Z$ are derived $I$-complete, so is the third. These assertions require neither finite generation of $I$ nor boundedness of the complexes.
